description:
This image displays two side-by-side false-colour satellite images acquired by Spot 5 (2.5 m resolution, 1/2/3 band combination) on 2011-07-23, illustrating the application of generalization rules for mapping low urban density areas. The images depict an agricultural area with scattered houses and a road network in Åre, Sweden.

The left panel shows the raw satellite imagery, where cultivated fields appear reddish-brown, and built-up areas and roads are cyan/white. The right panel shows the same area with green polygons overlayed, demonstrating the generalized delineation of urban fabric. These polygons encompass individual buildings and connecting road segments, merging them into larger continuous features. Two grey-filled labels within the polygons read "1110", which corresponds to "low urban density area class 1.1.1" as described in the accompanying text. Two yellow arrows indicate how previously separate structures or clusters are connected by this generalization.

This visualization exemplifies the exceptions from strict Minimum Mapping Unit (MMU) and Minimum Mapping Width (MMW) rules for urban areas, where a less restrictive MMW of less than 50 metres is applied at the urban fringe to ensure a more comprehensive representation of low urban density areas.
